svg.aria-label: Evaluation methods: from cheap checks to human judgment
svg.title: Evaluation methods: from cheap checks to human judgment
svg.desc: A ladder of five rows bottom to top. Row 1: programmatic evaluation, built-in or custom datasets with computed metrics like accuracy, stability, toxicity; cheap and repeatable on a fixed dataset. Row 2: LLM-as-a-judge, a model grading outputs on correctness, completeness, faithfulness, harmfulness, refusal quality, and style; human-like judgment at scale. Row 3: human evaluation, your employees or an AWS-managed team; the bar is relevance, style, brand voice. Row 4: bring-your-own-inference, evaluate any model or full app response even outside Bedrock. Row 5: RAG evaluation, retrieval relevance plus generation faithfulness, powered by LLM-as-a-judge, to prove the RAG system does not hallucinate. A footer says all of these run as a Bedrock model evaluation job.
svg.text: EVAL LADDER: CLIMB FROM CHEAP CHECKS TO HUMAN JUDGMENT
proves the system does not hallucinate
evaluate any model or full app
system under test is not a Bedrock call
your team or an AWS-managed team
All of these run as a Bedrock model evaluation job. The demo looked good is not a release criterion: models regress on prompt changes.
